title: A Compass for the Uniform
premise: In the tidal port of Greyhaven, Ivo Brightwater has spent nine years as an invisible clerk for the Meridian Trading Company, convinced that history is something that happens to bolder people. When a half-drowned stranger, Sefa, washes up carrying letters in the handwriting of Captain Aldous Vane—a man officially lost at sea and secretly the company's founder—she and Ivo realize the documents prove Vane faked his death to escape embezzlement charges that were pinned on innocent sailors. Racing three checkpoints before the morning tide, they must smuggle the evidence aboard the very ship meant to destroy it, discovering along the way that belonging sometimes means choosing each other over safety. The story ends with the letters delivered to a magistrate at sea, the company's directors arrested, and Ivo—no longer indentured, no longer invisible—sailing out with Sefa toward a history they now write themselves.
about_author: Mara Thornbury spent a decade cataloguing maritime archives in coastal England before turning to fiction, where her love of tide charts and forgotten ledgers shapes every page. She writes from a converted pilot's cottage, convinced that the most ordinary lives hold the most extraordinary testimony.

chapters.title: The Weight of Ordinary Days
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. We meet Greyhaven's docks, the Meridian Company's ledgers, and Ivo's careful philosophy of invisibility—keep your head down, copy your figures, want nothing. A quiet humiliation by the harbormaster establishes the cost of being nobody. Emotional beat: numb resignation mistaken for peace.

chapters.title: A Stranger on the Mudflats
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At dawn, Ivo finds Sefa half-drowned among the oyster beds, clutching an oilskin packet she refuses to surrender even unconscious. Hiding her in the counting-house loft, Ivo glimpses the letters: unmistakable handwriting from a dead man. Emotional beat: first crack in Ivo's armor—curiosity, then fear.

chapters.title: Handwriting of the Drowned
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Recovering, Sefa explains she served aboard the Meridian flagship; Captain Vane, presumed lost with all hands, wrote these letters naming the directors who framed him—and who now plan to burn every record before the audit ship arrives. Emotional beat: Sefa's grief and fury, and her wary assessment of Ivo as ally or liability.

chapters.title: What the Ledgers Confess
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Cross-checking Sefa's letters against nine years of entries, Ivo finds the falsified manifests in their own hand-copied pages—the company used them as an unwitting accomplice. The realization that invisibility made them complicit shatters their philosophy. Emotional beat: guilt transmuted into resolve.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. Sefa maps the route to the audit vessel anchored beyond the harbor chain: the gatehouse guard, the customs shed, and Director Corvane himself inspecting cargo at the quay. She proposes smuggling the packet inside a shipment of pearl shell—Ivo's father's old trade. Emotional beat: reluctant partnership hardening into trust.

chapters.title: The Gatehouse Bargain
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. At the first checkpoint, Ivo trades on years of being overlooked, but the gate sergeant—a childhood friend—recognizes them and must choose whether to sound the alarm. He looks away, at terrible personal risk. Emotional beat: the discovery that Ivo was never as unseen as they believed; people were watching all along.

chapters.title: Fire in the Customs Shed
chapters.summary: Sefa's POV. At the second checkpoint, customs officers grow suspicious and begin opening crates. Sefa creates a diversion—a small fire in the tar stores—and the packet passes in the chaos, but she is recognized and pursued. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration; Sefa realizes she's fighting not just for justice but for a future worth having.

chapters.title: Corvane's Offer
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. Director Corvane intercepts Ivo at the quay, revealing he's known about the letters since the stranger arrived. He offers freedom papers, wealth, and erasure of their complicity—if they hand over the packet and let the ship sail clean. Emotional beat: the theme crystallized—power corrupts by making survival the price of conscience.

chapters.title: The Morning Tide
chapters.summary: Alternating POV, climax. Ivo appears to accept Corvane's bargain, boarding the ship with the packet—then reveals it hidden in plain sight among the magistrate's own sealed dispatches, which Ivo, as a trusted clerk, was summoned to deliver. Sefa holds off Corvane's men at the gangway. The anchor lifts as the truth reaches the audit vessel. Emotional beat: love against duty—each chooses the other and the truth over safety.

chapters.title: A Compass for the Uniform
chapters.summary: Shared POV, resolution. Directors arrested at anchor; the indentured clerks freed by the magistrate's writ. Ivo, offered reinstatement, declines—instead signing aboard a survey ship with Sefa as navigator. The title's meaning lands: a compass doesn't tell you where to go, only how to hold your course. Emotional beat: belonging found not in a place or a company, but in a shared direction.
